MonogenicPrimaryMention.description:
IBD is monogenic in origin and the genetic defect is the disease
(e.g., IL10R deficiency, NEMO deficiency presenting as monogenic IBD).

Do not extract family history or carrier status.
Do not use this field for pharmacogenomic testing such as TPMT or NUDT15.

clinical_significance.description: Documented primary monogenic or syndromic genetic cause of the patient's IBD. PATHOGENIC: pathogenic variant/disease-causing genetic IBD diagnosis; LIKELY_PATHOGENIC: likely pathogenic variant is documented as explaining IBD; UNCERTAIN: uncertain genetic finding or VUS is mentioned but not confirmed causal of IBD; LIKELY_BENIGN: likely benign finding documented; BENIGN: benign finding documented; NONE_OF_THE_ABOVE: no monogenic IBD cause is documented.

gene_symbol.description: Gene symbol for the monogenic IBD finding, if stated, normalized to an uppercase HGNC-style gene symbol when possible, such as IL10RA, IL10RB, XIAP, FOXP3, TTC7A, LRBA, CTLA4, STAT3, STAT1, NCF2, or CYBB. Use null if no monogenic IBD gene is stated.
gene_symbol.title: Gene Symbol

MonogenicSecondaryMention.description:
IBD or IBD-like intestinal inflammation documented as
secondary to a monogenic or syndromic genetic disorder.

Capture only when the note explicitly states that the patient's IBD,  enterocolitis, colitis, or
intestinal inflammation is secondary to or caused by an underlying monogenic disorder,
immune dysregulation syndrome, or genetic syndrome.

Do not use this field for pharmacogenomic testing such as TPMT or NUDT15.

has_mention.title: Has Mention

spans.description: The verbatim text where this concept was mentioned.

clinical_significance.description: Whether the patient's IBD or IBD-like intestinal inflammation is documented as secondary to a monogenic or syndromic genetic disorder. PATHOGENIC: pathogenic genetic diagnosis is documented as causing or explaining the intestinal disease. LIKELY_PATHOGENIC: likely pathogenic genetic diagnosis is documented as causing or explaining the intestinal disease. UNCERTAIN: uncertain genetic finding or VUS is mentioned but not confirmed causal. LIKELY_BENIGN: likely benign finding documented. BENIGN: benign finding documented. NONE_OF_THE_ABOVE: no monogenic or syndromic secondary cause of IBD is documented.

gene_symbol.description: Gene symbol for the secondary monogenic IBD finding, if stated, normalized to an uppercase HGNC-style gene symbol when possible, such as CYBB, NCF1, NCF2, NCF4 (CGD), FOXP3 (IPEX), WAS (Wiskott-Aldrich), XIAP, BIRC4 (XLP-2), STAT1, STAT3, DOCK8 (CMC/hyper-IgE), LRBA, CTLA4.
gene_symbol.title: Gene Symbol

PharmacogenomicsMention.description:
Patient's TPMT or NUDT15 result, simplified for thiopurine dosing safety.

Capture results reported as metabolizer status (e.g., normal/intermediate/poor),
enzyme activity (e.g., low/normal TPMT activity), or genotype (e.g., TPMT *1/*1,
TPMT *1/*3A). All three routes inform the same dosing decision.

Examples:
* "TPMT normal metabolizer" -> NORMAL

* "TPMT intermediate metabolizer" -> ABNORMAL
* "TPMT *1/*3A, reduced activity" -> ABNORMAL
* "low TPMT activity" -> ABNORMAL
* "NUDT15 intermediate metabolizer" -> ABNORMAL
* "TPMT pending" -> NONE_OF_THE_ABOVE

Do not extract family history of IBD, negated IBD, rule-out IBD, or suspected/probable/working-diagnosis IBD.
Do not extract pending or carrier-only TPMT/NUDT15 results.

metabolizer_status.description: Simplified TPMT or NUDT15 result. NORMAL: normal metabolizer, normal enzyme activity, or wild-type genotype such as TPMT *1/*1. ABNORMAL: intermediate or poor metabolizer, reduced or absent enzyme activity, or any non-wild-type genotype documented as altering thiopurine metabolism. NONE_OF_THE_ABOVE: no TPMT or NUDT15 result is documented.

gene_symbol.description: Thiopurine-relevant gene tested, as TPMT or NUDT15. Use null if no specific gene is named.
gene_symbol.title: Gene Symbol
